question: Treating B12-deficiency megaloblastic anaemia with folic acid alone is dangerous because folic acid corrects the haematological abnormality but does not prevent or may worsen the neurological deterioration of subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The folic acid trap is a critical clinical safety point: folic acid can mask B12 deficiency haematologically while allowing neurological damage (SACD) to progress undetected. Always check serum B12 before starting folate supplementation in megaloblastic anaemia.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the 'folic acid trap': folic acid bypasses the B12-dependent methionine synthase step in DNA synthesis, correcting the macrocytic anaemia. However, B12 deficiency in the methylmalonyl-CoA pathway continues to cause myelin damage. Never give folic acid without first ruling out B12 deficiency.
